en: The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Six Times a Householder’s Son Left Home, translated by the Song Dynasty śramaṇa Shi Huijian.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Bhagavān was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.

At that time, the elder’s son Saṅgharakṣita, having gone forth from home to follow the path up to six times, went to where the World-Honored One was, prostrated with his head at the Buddha’s feet, and stood to one side.
Then the householder’s son Saṅgharakṣita addressed the World-Honored One, saying:
“May the World-Honored One grant me permission to leave the household life and study the Path. Thereupon, Saṅgharakṣita was permitted to leave the household life and study the Path.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the bhikṣu Saṃgharakṣita:
"You should practice two dharmas. What are these two?"
"Śamatha and vipaśyanā are these.
The bhikṣu Saṃgharāma addressed the Buddha, saying:
"I have understood well, World-Honored One!"
“You have understood the Tathāgata very well!
The World-Honored One said, “I have spoken by way of essentials; why do you say that you have understood very well?”
Saṅgharakkhita addressed the Buddha, saying:
“Cessation, Blessed One, is the eternal stilling of all fetters; contemplation is the contemplation of all phenomena.
The Blessed One replied:
“Excellent, excellent, Saṅgharakṣama!
You have taken up the essential teaching I have spoken and are able to explain it in detail.”

Then Saṃgharakṣita immediately received this instruction from the Buddha and contemplated its meaning in a secluded place. Having contemplated its meaning in that secluded place, the son of noble family shaved off his hair and beard, donned the three dharma-robes, and with firm faith went forth from home to study the Way. He cultivated the unsurpassed holy life, brought an end to the source of birth and death, established the holy life, accomplished what was to be done, and shall no longer receive a mother’s womb.
At that time, the Venerable Saṅgharakkhita attained the fruit of arhatship.

Now, while Saṅgharakkhita had not yet gone forth, his wife’s mother was still living; she heard that her daughter’s husband, the householder’s son Saṅgharakkhita, had gone forth under the Tathāgata and practiced the holy life for seven successive lifetimes, no longer indulging in sensual desires and having abandoned his household affairs and servants.
Then, Saṅgharakṣita’s mother-in-law took her daughter and went to where the bhikṣu Saṅgharakṣita was; she stood silently before him, sighed repeatedly, and spoke these words:
“O Saṅgharakṣita!...”

"Without propriety or decorum, and with improper thoughts, you have abandoned my daughter to go forth and study the Way under the Tathāgata. All the kings, great ministers, elders, brahmins, and kṣatriyas of Śrāvastī who have seen my daughter have been utterly infatuated and know not her whereabouts; they constantly harbor respectful thoughts and wish to dwell with her. Yet you, failing to reflect, have cast my daughter aside."
Then the Venerable Saṅgharakkhita spoke these verses:
"Beyond this there is nothing more essential; beyond this there is nothing comparable;
beyond this there is nothing further to be contemplated; no wise reflection surpasses this."
At that time, the mother of the Venerable Saṅgharakṣita’s wife said to Saṅgharakṣita:
“What fault or what transgression was there in my daughter’s mind?”
"Then why did you cause me to be abandoned and to go forth under the Tathāgata to study the Path?
At that time, the Venerable Saṅgharakkhita spoke these verses:
"Speaking evil words and constantly slandering, Envious and harboring a treacherous heart,"
"Hatred, delighting in false speech—these the Tathāgata calls great evils.

At that time, the wife and mother-in-law of the Venerable Saṅgharakkhita gazed at him from head to foot, and the bhikkhu likewise gazed at them from feet to head. Then the Venerable Saṅgharakkhita said:
"May the Venerable One accept my confession for the foolishness I have committed and my failure to distinguish the truth."
Saṅgharakṣita said, "May you, sister,
always be at peace and may your life be long. Then,
Saṅgharakṣita’s wife spoke to her mother, saying:
“Since Saṃgharakṣita calls me ‘sister,’ he will certainly no longer take pleasure in desire.
She then said to Saṃgharakṣita,
“May the Venerable Saṃgharakṣita accept my confession for what was done out of folly and ignorance, as I failed to distinguish the truth.”
Saṅgharakṣita said, "May you, sister,
be at peace and may your life be long.
Then Saṅgharakṣita’s wife and her mother bowed their heads at his feet, circumambulated him three times, sighed repeatedly, and withdrew.
Then, the Venerable Ānanda saw from afar, as he was leaving the city of Śrāvastī, the wife and mother-in-law of the Venerable Saṃgharakṣita; having seen them, he spoke these words:
"Sisters, have you seen Saṃgharakṣita?"
The wife of Saṅgharakkhita replied,
"I have seen Saṅgharakkhita and even conversed with him, yet my wish has not been fulfilled.
At that time, the Venerable Ānanda departed in silence.

Then the Venerable Ānanda returned to his own quarters, gathered up his robes and bowl, washed his hands and feet, placed his sitting mat (niṣīdana) over his shoulder, and went to where the World-Honored One was. He prostrated with his head at the Buddha’s feet, sat to one side, and after a short while withdrew to sit back down, reporting the matter in detail to the World-Honored One.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke these verses:
"To seek sprouts from a rotten tree, To seek drops of water within fire,
To seek fire within water— So it is to seek desire where there is no desire."
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the bhikṣus:
“Among my śrāvakas, the foremost bhikṣu capable of subduing Māra is the bhikṣu Saṃgharakṣita.”
At that time, the bhikṣus, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
This concludes the *Sūtra on the Six Times a Householder’s Son Left the Home Life* as spoken by the Buddha.
